text.insert: Capture the full pull-request history of the selected upstream decompilation repository into the game's local source archive. Include open, closed, and merged PRs so initial librarian backfill can research both accepted changes and unsuccessful approaches. Downloading the archive and curating knowledge from it are separate steps.

. Bind it through a game-relative script symlink in config/tools and reference that binding in scope.acquisition_script. It requires an explicit repository and archive directory. Legacy Melee acquisition remains separate until its configuration is migrated.

Each PR capture includes metadata and body text, issue comments, review comments, reviews, and the diff. Preserve repository identity and PR number with the evidence. PR numbers alone are not unique across repositories.
One PR can require several paginated API requests. GitHub primary and secondary rate limits can therefore make a full archive take multiple sessions. Start with modest
concurrency. If GitHub reports a limit, pause until its retry or reset time and lower concurrency before retrying. The fetcher does not implement automatic rate-limit backoff.
Keep the same archive directory when resuming. A manual rerun without
skips records whose required local files are present. The source pipeline currently requests
, so it can recapture existing records. The fetcher's
delay applies to its serial path, not to the concurrent worker pool.

Verify discovered PR numbers against the remote inventory, compare captured comment counts with PR metadata, and inspect per-PR diff errors. The shared helper retries records with diff.err. When GitHub rejects a diff for exceeding its file limit, it fetches the recorded commits into a bare cache inside the game's archive and generates a merge-base diff. Each fallback keeps its base, head, merge base, and API error in diff-provenance.json. The legacy Melee fetcher checks file presence and can count a failed diff as present.

After verifying capture, extract code targets before importing PR relationships. The current importer creates records for merged PRs that resolve to known targets or translation units; open, rejected, and unresolved PRs remain archived. Build keyword and embedding indexes with the selected game's archive. Keep archive coverage, imported relationships, search coverage, and librarian curation distinct.
